parts.instruction: You will hear three different extracts. For questions 1-6, choose the answer (A, B or C) which fits best

options.label: Nobody will listen to his complaints at work.
There is friction between him and a colleague.
He’s fallen out with his boss.
He needs to approach the problem in a different way.
He has to accept that there will be problems in any office.
He is the main cause of all the office problems.

questions.prompt: What were Janet’s expectations of the recruitment fair?

options.label: She was hoping to get some ideas for a career.
She was sure that someone would offer her a job in Public Relations.
She had incorrect preconceptions as to what she would gain from it.

questions.prompt: How did Paul gain from the recruitment fair?

options.label: He passed an interview there and got a job.
He impressed someone who then recommended him for a job.
He applied for several jobs there and was successful.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about his job?

options.label: You need to have a degree to get a promotion.
If you want a promotion you will have to go into management.
it’s a career that offers incentives for industrious people.

questions.prompt: What is the woman’s opinion of the man?

options.label: He is both courageous and mad.
He must have a cruel side to him.
His desire to get a promotion is more important than anything else

parts.instruction: You will hear a woman talking about her job as a probation worker. For questions 7-14, complete the sentences.

questions.prompt: Georgia didn’t think she had enough ________ for a career in probation work. .
While studying for her degree, Georgia worked as a ________ in three different places.
Being able to work out which ________ is the most urgent is an important skill.
While working face to face with an offender, you both have ________ to deal with.
Georgia works in the prison, ________ and her office.
The worst part of Georgia’s job is dealing with ________.
Georgia has to work with the courts to decide on a fair ________ for each offender.

parts.instruction: You will hear part of a radio interview with an economist. For questions 15-20, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which fits best according to what you hear.

options.label: women would need to work into their eighties to earn as much money as men.
good qualifications aren’t necessarily rewarded with high wages.
women will never earn as much as men.
more women have degrees than men.

questions.prompt: What is said about careers advice in schools?

options.label: it has been improved but it is still inadequate.
It is now quite good for girls but boys are being neglected.
There is no advice for girls that are ambitious.
Girls are always encouraged not to be ambitious.
women are to blame for not insisting on higher wages.
new government policies have solved most of the problems.
there is nothing more the government can do.
women shouldn’t necessarily be encouraged to change their choice of career

questions.prompt: A London School of Economics report showed that

options.label: women who worked part-time found it difficult to get a full-time job later on.
after having children, women find it harder to earn as much money as men.
women find it hard to find a job after having children.
most women want a full-time job after having a child.

questions.prompt: What does the ‘stuffed shirt’ policy mean?

options.label: Women are being forced to choose between family commitments and work.
Only men can have part-time senior positions
Women don’t get the opportunity to train for high-powered jobs.
No woman can have a senior position.
women should stay at home and look after their children.
women now earn as much money as men in the workplace.
women have been disadvantaged by outdated work ethics.
having children w ill soon be an advantage for working women.
